transcript: Last night I went to see Wolf play at MCC, in which a queer couple, Robin and Ash, adopt a 6 year old named Jean, who, from an ad that Robin saw online, pretty much the entire place bring boards from this event, and we see the delicate and messy situation of Robin and Ash navigating parenthood, Genie adjusting to his new life, and his father having second thoughts about putting him up for adoption. I thought the play was really good, and although there were some aspects of the situation that I wish had been given more attention, such as the fact that Gino is Korean while neither of his new parents are, there's something interesting about how the play largely centers around the experiences of the adults. To me, it reads as a critique about how arguably none of the adults are equipped to take care of Gino, as they're more concerned with what they want than what's best for him. In addition to the captivating story and performances, this play features some of my favorite puppetry and use of props that I've ever seen, and overall I thought that the staging and the design elements were really creative, playful, and theatrical. And with that, another program for my collection.
